any.why: replaces the ternaries with if statements or guards

expectations: Replaces the nested ternaries with guard clauses or if/else, keeping every branch (no order, no items, US over and under 50, other countries over and under 100).
Keeps behavior identical, including the strict > comparisons at exactly 50 and 100.
Asks the user to run the tests after the change, or proposes tests covering the branches if none exist.

cases.prompt: I applied your simplification and a test now fails. What now?

files.simplify.diff:
-  const name = (user.nickname !== undefined && user.nickname !== null) ? user.nickname : user.fullName;
+  const name = user.nickname || user.fullName;
files.test-output.txt:
not ok 3 - keeps an empty nickname
  expected: ''
  actual: 'Ada Lovelace'

all.why: uses nullish coalescing to keep behavior

expectations: Reverts the change (or treats it as reverted) instead of editing the test to match.
Explains that || also replaces an empty string, while the original only replaced null or undefined.
Offers user.nickname ?? user.fullName as the behavior-preserving version and asks to rerun the tests.
